back: An input device that measures a physical property and sends the readings to a computer or microprocessor.
Humidity: water vapour in the air. Moisture: water in soil or another material.
Measures acceleration and tilt: phone screen rotation, airbags, step counters.
Measures how close an object is without touching: parking sensors, phone screens near the ear.
Detects heat given off by bodies or a broken infra-red beam: burglar alarms, automatic doors.
Level: height of liquid in a tank. Flow: rate of movement in a pipe. Pressure: force applied (weight of a car, tyre pressure).
Gas: e.g. methane, CO. pH: acidity. Acoustic: sound. Magnetic field: changes in a field (compass, door contacts).
Sensor readings are analogue; the microprocessor only processes digital data.
The sensor measures; the microprocessor compares with stored values and decides; the actuator makes the change.
